title.rendered: Into Your Hands I Commit My Spirit | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 14

excerpt.rendered: The last recorded prayer of Jesus’ earthly life was spoken from the cross. One sentence, drawn from Psalm 31, prayed every evening by Jewish children before sleep. The ultimate expression of entrustment.

content.rendered:
The last recorded prayer of Jesus’ earthly life was spoken from the cross. One sentence, drawn from Psalm 31, prayed every evening by Jewish children before sleep. On Good Friday afternoon Jesus prayed it one final time, in a loud voice, and gave up His spirit. This is where the series ends. And where the believer’s prayer life begins.

The Gospel For Today | Friday, October 16, 2026 | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 14

Today’s Scripture

“And when Jesus had cried out with a loud voice, He said, ‘Father, into Your hands I commit My spirit.’ Having said this, He breathed His last.”
Luke 23:46 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

It was the ninth hour. Three in the afternoon. Jesus had hung on the cross for six hours. The darkness that had covered the land from noon was beginning to lift. The cup He had asked in Gethsemane to let pass had been drunk to the bottom. The sins of the world had been laid on Him. The wrath of God against all human rebellion had been poured out on Him. The cry “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?” had already come. The scripture of John 19:28 had been fulfilled: “It is finished.” And now, in the final moments of His earthly life, Jesus prayed one last recorded prayer. One sentence. Drawn from Psalm 31, verse 5, the evening prayer that every Jewish child was taught by their mother before sleep. “Into Your hand I commit my spirit.” Jesus prayed it with a loud voice, Luke tells us. Not a whisper. Not the exhausted murmur of a dying man. A loud voice. Then He breathed His last.

The prayer was the completion of everything the previous thirteen days of this series have been pointing toward. Jesus had taught His disciples to pray with authority. He had taught them to speak to mountains, to still storms, to raise the dead, to intercede for the body of Christ, to submit in Gethsemane. And now, in His final breath, He modelled the ultimate expression of all of it. The complete entrustment of His entire self into the hands of the Father. Not with uncertainty. Not with fear of what the Father would do. With the full confidence of a Son who knew the Father perfectly, and knew the Father’s hands were the safest place in the universe for His spirit to be. The resurrection that would come on Sunday morning was already secured in the trustworthiness of the Hands He committed Himself into on Friday afternoon.

The Passion Translation renders the moment with the weight of its finality: “Then Jesus shouted out with a loud passionate cry to his Father, saying, ‘Father, into your hands I surrender my spirit.’ And he took his last breath and died” (Luke 23:46 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “And Jesus, crying out with a loud voice, said, Father, into Your hands I commit My spirit! And with these words, He expired” (Luke 23:46 AMPC). Expired. Breathed His last. The Son handed Himself fully to the Father. And the Father received Him. Three days later, those same Hands would raise Him from the dead, exalt Him to the right hand of the Majesty on High, and seat Him far above every principality and power.

How Jesus Prayed

The Format. One sentence. A quoted psalm. Spoken loudly. Final. The format itself preached a sermon. Even in death, Jesus prayed scripture. Even in the last breath, Jesus prayed to the Father. The believer learns that the end of life is still a praying life, and the Word of God is still the believer’s prayer book.

The Essence. Total entrustment. Jesus did not die trying to save Himself. He did not die trying to control the outcome. He died handing His entire spirit into the Father’s hands. The essence of mature Christian prayer is the same movement, practised day by day throughout the believer’s life. Not clutching. Not controlling. Entrusting.

The Authority. Here is the stunning paradox. The entrustment prayer of Luke 23:46 is the gateway to all the authority this series has been teaching. The believer who learns to commit everything into the Father’s hands walks in the greatest spiritual authority. The one who refuses to let go of self cannot wield the authority Jesus delegated. The authority is reserved for the surrendered.

The Assurance. “Father.” Even in the hour of being made sin for us, Jesus called Him Father. The relationship was perfectly restored by the time the final prayer was spoken. The forsakenness of the three hours of darkness was finished. The sin had been dealt with. The Father was Father again. The believer who prays this prayer prays it from the same restored relationship purchased on Jesus’ cross.

The Submission. This is the ultimate submission. Not just a cup, not just a season, not just a decision. The entire spirit. The whole self. Everything. For the believer, this is the daily surrender that undergirds every other prayer. Everything the believer is, has, hopes for, or fears, is handed daily into the hands of the Father. Then the believer is free to pray with authority, because self is out of the way.

The Result. Jesus breathed His last. The veil of the Temple tore from top to bottom. The centurion at the foot of the cross confessed, “Truly this Man was the Son of God!” The sun returned. The earth shook. The tombs opened. And on the third morning, the Father answered the prayer by raising Jesus from the dead and seating Him at His right hand. The entrustment was received. The exaltation followed. For Gospelbuzz readers today, wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, this is where fourteen days of learning to pray lands. In the Father’s hands. Everything you are. Everything you have. Everything you are trusting Him for. Place it there today. And then rise and walk in the authority of One who learned to pray the way Jesus prayed.

Prayer (Pattern After Jesus)

Address. Father. My Father. Through the finished work of Jesus I come freely into Your presence, bought by His blood, sealed by Your Spirit, welcomed as a son/daughter.

Entrustment. Into Your hands I commit my spirit. Into Your hands I commit this day. Into Your hands I commit my family, my work, my health, my future, my finances, my fears, my dreams. Everything I am, everything I have, I place into Your hands today.

Confession. Your hands are the safest place in the universe. I release my grip. I stop clutching. I stop trying to control what only You can hold.

Walking in Authority. From this entrusted place, Father, I rise to walk in the authority Jesus has placed on me. I will speak to mountains in His name. I will pray for the sick in His name. I will intercede for those in my care. I will declare Your Kingdom today, free of self, grounded in surrender, moving in Your Spirit.

In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I have learned to pray as Jesus prayed. My spirit is committed into the Father’s hands. From that place of entrustment, I rise to walk in the authority of Christ. I speak to mountains. I calm storms. I command sickness to leave. I raise the dead things in my life. I intercede for those around me. I submit my will to the Father’s. I pray as a Son of the Living God.
